item1.justification: The examiner consistently applies Graham/KSR factors (scope and content, differences, PHOSITA level, secondary considerations) for all §103 rejections, with no misapplication of §101 or other statutory frameworks.

item2.justification: All rejections cite specific prior art (US-2013159180-A1) and map its disclosed features (lien facility, pre-configured timing, portal/channel communication, wallet journal) to specific claim limitations throughout the novelty, obviousness, and office action stages.

item3.justification: The §102 novelty findings and §103 obviousness conclusions are consistent — claims found novel at §102 (8, 17, 19, 20) are also found non-obvious, and claims found not novel are generally found obvious, with no unexplained reversals between stages.

item4.justification: With strictness=0.422 (moderate-low), the examiner appropriately resolves ambiguous cases (claims 1, 10, 19, 20, 21) toward a middle ground — rejecting most claims while noting non-obvious allowable subject matter in claims 8 and 17, and recommending amendment rather than outright denial, consistent with a lenient-to-neutral pragmatist profile.

item5.justification: The final decision of 'amend_suggested' with rejection of most claims and allowance of claims 8/17 follows directly from the accumulated stage analyses, which consistently identified those claims as the only ones lacking prior art disclosure throughout the novelty and obviousness stages.
